Correctness check: Light speed ~300,000 km/s, sound ~343 m/s, both correct. Dividing the seconds by 3 gives km (343 m/s means about 3 s per km), and dividing by 5 gives miles (about 4.7 s per mile), so both are correct. The 15 s example gives 5 km or 3 miles, which is correct.

Safety tip: a 30-second gap corresponds to about 10 km, or 6 miles. The standard "30-30 rule" says to seek shelter if the gap is under 30 seconds and to wait 30 minutes after the last thunder. This is correct. "Within about 10 km or 6 miles" is consistent.
